title: Case-insensitive account identifier removal from retained audit text
classification: Confirmed privacy leak fixed: an unlinked PostgreSQL audit event containing a case-variant account email escaped the prior case-sensitive selector.
change: Retained audit event lookup now uses SQLAlchemy icontains with autoescape, so case variants are selected while SQL wildcard characters in identifiers remain literal. Matching identifier text is then replaced case-insensitively.

verification.reproduction: The new PostgreSQL regression failed before the fix because the case-variant email remained in retained SystemEvents.event_text after account deletion.
verification.result: passed: 5 tests on Python 3.14.10 and PostgreSQL 17.6
verification.database: Fresh oneirodexr1978test database upgraded from Alembic baseline through head; dropped after verification. TEST_DATABASE_URL and DATABASE_URL were process-scoped overrides; root .env unchanged.

coverage: the existing audit event remains but no longer contains the deleted user's name, email or user ID
an unlinked security event with the email in different letter case is also anonymized
absolute Windows, UNC and POSIX paths in retained audit text are redacted
the account-deletion module's Flask, native mutation, file cleanup and ASGI restart cases pass
limits: The PostgreSQL test uses the current Alembic schema, not a deployed operator schema.
The review covers retained SystemEvents text; other retained user-authored free-text fields still need classification.
